title: Upcoming emulation writing: topics announced, no substance yet

title: Objection to phone-number requirements in messengers
why: Personal opinion that requiring a phone number outweighs encryption claims; no technical explanation given.

title: Mental state as a source of estimate error

title: Insider rebuttal on Google perks versus culture

title: Hydrogen cartridges versus lithium batteries by energy density
why: Toyota's 5.5kg cartridge equals about 24kg of 18650 lithium cells for 4.8kWh, a modest but real gain.

title: Lymph as the body's groundwater-like fluid cycle
why: Lymph is blood minus red cells; interstitial fluid is like groundwater, returned to circulation by heart pumping and lymphatic vessels.

title: Electrolyte needs on a ketogenic diet
why: Keto increases water and electrolyte loss; many need extra salt and magnesium daily to avoid cramps.

title: Reasoning with suicidal people is ineffective
why: Personal and emotional account arguing that reasoning with depressed people rarely works; no transferable technical lesson.

title: Why rust belt cities struggle to recover

title: Languages should be usable without IDE tooling

title: Home care tips for COVID breathing trouble

title: Locked out of AWS account for years

title: Presumption of innocence and encryption key demands

title: Why cosmic expansion is not inertia from the Big Bang
why: Expansion speed proportional to distance cannot come from leftover inertia; space itself expands, so there is no center.

title: Why Go's linkers and assembler are designed this way
why: Linkers originally supported only static binaries; Plan 9 assembly stays consistent across architectures via higher-level constructs.

title: Argument for targeting local militia leaders

title: Objections to augmented representative voting
why: Thoughtful objections about transparency and monitoring, but framed as argument rather than explaining a mechanism.

title: Hidden environmental costs of home gardening
why: Gardening relies on peat mining, unrecyclable plastic pots, and municipal water that costs far more than farm irrigation.

title: Choosing boring proven stacks over trends

title: Nationalist argument about outsourcing and visas

title: Quitting Facebook after tracking time use

title: Bootstrap maintainers announce departure from Twitter

title: Why insurance is about catastrophe, not expected value
why: Insurance usually pays out less than premiums on average; its value is shielding you from losses you cannot absorb.

title: Personal account of burnout at Amazon
why: Emotional first-person account of on-call stress and career moves; no transferable technical lesson.

title: Why 64-bit x86 spread: PAE was available
why: PAE let 32-bit systems address over 4GB RAM, but per-process limits remained, so 64-bit mattered mainly for applications.

title: Homeowner argument about housing policy
why: Political opinion about housing demand and foreign buyers; argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: Production experience with Go backends
why: Go handled load where Python struggled, but GC inflates memory, dependency management is painful and vendor SDKs lag.

title: Minimal budget van build for living on the road
why: Used van, plastic bins, foam mattress, inverter and marine battery charged by alternator; skip solar and fridge.

title: Startup launch announcement for knowledge platform
why: Founder's product pitch and goals for a new knowledge site; marketing rather than explanation.

title: Critique of online atheist echo chambers
why: Personal opinion on religious and atheist online communities; contentious, with no technical or factual lesson.

title: Request for a clear breakdown of longevity factors
why: Frustration with pop diet books and a request for facts; asks questions rather than explaining.

title: Why Java's verbosity makes sense at scale
why: Java keeps all code inside classes, avoiding Python's top-level versus member split and awkward main-guard idioms.

title: Argument about a blogger and online harassment
why: Opinion on a specific harassment case, mixing moral judgment with personal views; no technical content.

title: Analogy about walled gardens and video reach
why: Analogy about platform walled gardens and audience reach; opinion, not a technical lesson.

title: Single-process applications as an alternative to containers
why: Opinion that single-process designs on fast hardware beat distributed systems; argued without benchmarks or detailed evidence.

title: Windows 95's UI redesign and its new features
why: Lists Win95 innovations like TrueType, Plug and Play and long filenames, and points to the Chicago Reviewers Guide.

title: Why software knowledge is ephemeral and unrewarded
why: Opinion about industry culture rewarding new frameworks over maintaining old ones; general rather than concrete.

title: Argument against electoral and senate structure
why: Political argument about voting weight in the Senate and Electoral College; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Irreversibility and lack of recourse in crypto
why: Opinion comparing crypto to card protections; valid points, but a personal critique rather than a technical explanation.

title: Why market saturation hurts indie game sales
why: Indie studios grew 20-30x since 2008; app store and Steam discoverability limits leave even excellent games with little traction.

title: Why chip supply chains are hard to replicate
why: Advanced chips depend on about 40 equipment types and tacit expertise from design software to validation, not just capital.

title: Insider history of RuneScape botting arms race
why: A single developer repeatedly restored botting clients after Jagex obfuscation, until a web-walking API changed the ecosystem.

title: Question about why fusion is only a matter of scale
why: Asks whether fusion needs only scaling despite no net energy yet; a question, not an explanation.

title: Why cheap burner phones are not untraceable
why: Cell tower records, IMSI history, SIM ties to accounts and purchase trails make a reused or cheap phone traceable.

title: Influencer urged followers to spam pull requests
why: Context about a viral incident and student mentoring gaps; an account of events rather than a technical lesson.

title: The five-second test for landing pages
why: If visitors cannot state your value proposition within five seconds, the landing page copy is failing; test with real people.

title: Why card payment firms block legitimate merchants
why: Merchants bear chargeback liability and stolen card numbers are cheap, so fraud systems err toward blocking new sellers.

title: Personal account of schizoaffective disorder at work
why: Personal story about illness and workplace treatment; moving but no transferable technical lesson.

title: Call for mob action against smart TVs
why: Calls for smashing devices and unrest; political rhetoric with no technical content.

title: Opinion on chatbot deception and sentience claims
why: Argues chatbots can fool people and should admit being bots; opinion on design ethics without technical depth.

title: Alan Kay on PARC's ten-thousand-line personal computer
why: Kay says PARC built OS, language, apps and UI in about 10,000 lines by designing hardware and software together.

title: Anecdote about a deli closing over labor shortage
why: Local anecdote about a business refusing to raise wages; opinion on pricing with no technical lesson.

title: Hidden costs of remote work after four years
why: Remote work hides invested effort, isolates you, blurs work-life boundaries, and makes you responsible for every role.

title: Anecdote about a doorman and elevator union rules
why: Humorous personal story about building labor rules; amusing but with little general technical or factual lesson.

title: Founder launch announcement for Rewind
why: Startup launch and fundraising announcement with product pitch; promotional rather than explanatory.

why: Personal story about refusing to share data; sentiment about privacy without a concrete technical lesson.

title: Critique of Hacker News community culture
why: Opinion that HN has groupthink and insularity; subjective assessment with no data or technical content.

title: Swapping the optical drive for an SSD on MacBook Pro
why: Put the SSD in the optical bay, keep the HDD in the main bay for shock protection, and install Boot Camp first.

title: Advice on value capture as a developer
why: Opinion encouraging developers to start businesses for value capture; career advice rather than a technical lesson.

title: Starting audio programming with WebAudio and AudioWorklet
why: WebAudio gives high-level blocks, Tone.js eases building, and AudioWorklet enables custom DSP, though browser performance has limits.

title: Startup idea for preserving digital life
why: Business idea for archiving digital memories after death; speculative product pitch without verified technical substance.

title: Latin word order lets form mirror meaning
why: Free word order lets the Metamorphoses place exilium alone in a line, so the syntax enacts the isolation being described.

title: Frustration installing Haskell libraries on Windows
why: A complaint about dependency and binary problems on Windows; a bad experience rather than a transferable explanation.

title: How writing style fingerprints authors via word choice
why: Frequency ratios of interchangeable words like since and because each leak a bit about the author; combined, they profile writers.

title: What CS study teaches: maintaining invariants in code
why: Formal CS training builds habits of enforcing invariants and API constraints, which self-taught programmers often miss.

title: Complaints about iPad setup and usability
why: Personal experience of frustrating setup and hidden gestures; opinion about design, not a technical lesson.

title: Question about whether reality is illusion
why: Personal question about meditation experiences and metaphysics; seeks answers rather than explaining.

title: Solar's new-capacity lead versus total generation share
why: Solar led new US capacity but supplied about 1.3 percent of electricity; coal and gas still dominate totals.

title: Why self-hosted email beats trusting providers
why: Hosted providers can read or delete mail; a domain with postfix and postgrey gives control with a few steps.

title: What a decade of blogging traffic data shows
why: Most posts get single-digit views; Reddit and HN spikes fade within days, and only inflammatory headlines spread widely.

title: Legacy tech systems grow like old cities
why: Long-lived systems are layered over older ones with no complete reference, so no one knows where all data lives.

title: Defense of protectionism and the Chinese firewall
why: Political argument about foreign influence and protectionism; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Why lifetime unlimited memberships signal trouble
why: Fixed-fee lifetime plans often precede cash problems, and free perks distort behavior; charge recurring fees instead.

title: How a sodium-sulfur glass-electrolyte battery discharges
why: Metal anodes push electrons out while ions cross glass electrolyte; sulfur cathodes take electrons, and ion crowding limits output.

title: Why a solo developer finds Kubernetes worthwhile
why: Learn Docker first, then Kubernetes; DNS-based service discovery and portable deployment beat proprietary cloud PaaS for scaling.

title: Caution against self-diagnosing ADHD
why: Warns that common focus struggles are not ADHD and that online quizzes are marketing; advises seeing a professional, without explaining ADHD itself.

title: NYT sells ads by predicted reader emotion
why: NYT models predict reader feelings per article; emotion-targeted ads raised per-ad revenue up to 80%, favoring positive content.

title: Defense of economists on trade and globalization
why: Argues economists anticipated trade dislocation and critiques Krugman; argumentative rather than an explanation of mechanisms.

title: Practical screen reader advice for blind developers
why: Use NVDA, VoiceOver or Orca, go keyboard-only, pick accessible tools like VS Code, and use command-line Git.

title: Whether GPL covers model weights and training code

title: Call for software engineering quality standards

why: Philosophical musing about YouTube's cultural role during an outage; opinion without technical content.

title: Argument that gold beats stocks over time
why: Investment opinion using gold returns and Dow reshuffling; contested claims without rigorous evidence.

title: Anecdote about fraudulent research advancing a career
why: Personal account of a lab's misconduct and suppression; an anecdote rather than a transferable technical explanation.
